note.title: Electric circuits, current and potential difference
note.overview: Circuit behaviour can be predicted using charge flow and energy transfer. Current describes charge flow, while potential difference describes energy transferred per unit charge.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Current is the rate of flow of electric charge and is measured in amperes (A).
An ammeter is connected in series with the component or branch being measured.
Potential difference is energy transferred per unit charge and is measured in volts (V).
A voltmeter is connected in parallel across a component.
A complete conducting loop is needed for sustained current.
Current is the same everywhere in a simple series circuit.
At a junction, total current entering equals total current leaving.
Potential differences across series components add to the supply; parallel branches have the same potential difference as the supply.
